Bound each coordinatewise sign-disagreement inner product by twice the absolute gradient coordinate times the disagreement indicator.

Drop the disagreement indicator and identify the l1 norm of the estimator error.

key_lemmas.ref: Lemma 1, p.5; Appendix A, p.14
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{For the update }x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta(\operatorname{sign}(v_t)+\lambda x_t),\text{ as long as the initial point satisfies }\|x_1\|_{\infty}\le\eta,\text{ we can ensure that each }x_t\text{ is bounded such that }\|x_t\|_{\infty}\le\eta t,\quad \|x_t\|^2\le 2\eta^2t^2d.\ \text{Additionally, by setting }\lambda\le\frac{1}{2\eta T},\text{ we can show that the update step is also bounded, i.e., }\|x_{t+1}-x_t\|^2\le4\eta^2d.
key_lemmas.role: Provides the iterate infinity-norm control needed to absorb weight decay and the update-step bound used in the smoothness and estimator-error recurrences.

proof.description: Rewrite x_t using the update rule one step back and take the l-infinity norm; the displayed coefficient (1-eta lambda) rather than |1-eta lambda| uses the paper's implicit nonnegative-contraction parameter domain flagged in source_gaps.
Unroll the l-infinity recursion over previous iterates and express the sign contribution by a maximum over i=1,...,t-1; this requires the same implicit nonnegative contraction 0 <= 1-eta lambda <= 1.

Use ||sign(v_i)||_infty <= 1, drop the contraction factor, and use the initial-point condition to obtain ||x_t||_infty <= eta t; dropping the factor relies on the implicit nonnegative-contraction domain.
Repeat the update-rule and triangle-inequality argument in the Euclidean norm, using ||sign(v_{t-1})|| <= sqrt(d), and unroll with the same implicit nonnegative-contraction domain.
Square the Euclidean bound, split the square into the initial and accumulated sign terms, and drop the contraction power using the implicit 0 <= 1-eta lambda <= 1 domain.
Convert ||x_1||^2 to ||x_1||_infty^2 d and use ||x_1||_infty <= eta to get the stated ||x_t||^2 bound.
Write the update displacement and split its square into the weight-decay part and sign part.
Substitute the iterate l2-squared bound ||x_t||^2 <= 2 eta^2 t^2 d into the update-displacement estimate.
Use Algorithm 1's finite horizon t <= T to replace t^2 by T^2 in the displayed chain.
Apply lambda <= 1/(2 eta T) to the horizon-bounded expression to conclude the stated update-step bound.

extension.request: Extend the existing centralized Lion project IN THE SAME Lion.lean and Lion.json with Algorithm 2 (v1), Theorem 3, Assumptions 5/7/8 and Appendix D. Reuse the existing centralized definitions and proofs; automatically identify adapters and genuinely new distributed obligations. Preserve the centralized statement-correction evidence. Explicitly justify sum versus average under sign, cross-node independence/noise cancellation, the 1/n variance improvement, and n/d/T-dependent schedules without silently adding source assumptions. Keep both centralized and distributed results in the same Lean file. Do not create another standalone distributed Setup or new Lean module unnecessarily. The earlier distributed JSON at /workspace/artifact/LionDistributed.json is read-only supplementary PDF extraction, not the base implementation or an approved Lean model. Exclude Algorithm 2 v2 and Algorithm 3.

reuse.reason: Algorithm 2 v1 uses the same coordinatewise sign plus weight-decay update as centralized Algorithm 1; only the source of the server direction is adapted. The target pointer is zero-based and resolves to the algorithm_spec object whose printed step field is 6, shared_sign_weight_decay_update.

The iterate and step bounds depend only on the shared x-update, so the centralized proof is reused after replacing the centralized direction by the distributed summed/averaged direction and carrying the same corrected eta-lambda domain.

Appendix D explicitly says the centralized descent analysis is valid through Eq. (5); the adapter changes the true gradient to the average objective and the estimator-error route to the distinct averaged estimator bar v_t, while the sign update is transported from the distributed server sum via positive scaling.
The distributed node v update is the centralized lookahead-momentum recurrence applied independently at each node; averaging worker errors and proving the 1/n noise reduction remain new obligations.
The distributed node m update is the centralized original-momentum recurrence applied independently at each node; the distributed averaging and cross-node variance argument are new obligations.

The proof trace establishes the finite-horizon bound immediately before the final schedule substitution; the asymptotic rate is recorded as a paper claim under the one-sided schedule notation, while a formally closed rate must additionally consume the derived corrected schedule contract TwoSidedSchedulePrerequisiteForRate.

proof.description: Appendix D reuses the Theorem 1 descent analysis through Eq. (5), now for the global distributed objective f. The displayed source formula overloads v_t; the formal adapter keeps Algorithm 2's server sum v_t^{\mathrm{sum}} separate and instantiates the reused descent bound with the averaged estimator \bar v_t. This instantiation relies on the positive-scaling sign bridge between the server sum and the averaged estimator, without equating their squared estimator errors. Phase 0 must instantiate the inherited corrected-domain declaration Algorithms.Unverified.Lion.lemma_one_iterate_and_step_bounds_correctedDomain, represented here by the inherited key lemma Lemma_1_IterateAndStepBounds together with the explicit eta-lambda domain obligation.

The PDF writes an equality with the symbol v_t on the left and (1/n) sum_j v_t^j on the right. This is a source inconsistency, not an equality between the squared errors of the server sum and the average. The formal route introduces v_t^{\mathrm{sum}} and \bar v_t=(1/n)v_t^{\mathrm{sum}}, uses the positive-scaling sign identity only to preserve the actual sign update, and replaces the estimator-error argument in the reused Eq. (5) adapter by \bar v_t. No statement of the form ||\nabla f-v_t^{\mathrm{sum}}||^2=||\nabla f-\bar v_t||^2 is made.
proof.ref: Appendix D, p.19; Algorithm 2, line 8, p.8

proof.description: For each worker, expand the next v-estimator error according to the v_t^j definition.
Average the per-worker expansion and use the global-gradient average identity.

Square the averaged v-error decomposition. The paper's first displayed Eq. (9) inequality separates the previous averaged m-error, the stochastic contribution already written as a sum of individual node-noise second moments, and the node-gradient drift. The passage from the averaged decomposition to this printed individual-variance term consumes the explicit cross-node cancellation prerequisite before the displayed source boundary; no summed-noise residual is carried forward. The 1/beta_1 Young-inequality coefficient also requires beta_1>0, which the PDF does not state separately from the momentum-order condition.

Apply Assumption 7 to the printed individual node-noise second moments and Assumption 5 to the node gradient drift, obtaining the next displayed Eq. (9) inequality. The retained 1/beta_1 denominator uses the unstated positive-domain prerequisite for beta_1.

Use Lemma 1's step bound to replace ||x_{t+1}-x_t||^2 by 4 eta^2 d, and use the global-gradient average identity to write the m-error against \nabla f(x_t). The Lemma 1 displacement substitution is instantiated on the Algorithm 2 horizon and consumes the explicit eta/lambda positivity-domain prerequisite; the beta_1 denominator is justified only under the momentum positive-domain prerequisite.

The same calculation with beta_2 and m_{t+1}^j gives the averaged m-error recursion, again instantiating Lemma 1's corrected-domain displacement bound over the Algorithm 2 horizon. As in Eq. (9), the displayed beta_2^2 sigma^2/n term uses cross-node noise cancellation not explicitly stated beyond Assumption 7, and the 1/beta_2 coefficient needs beta_2>0.

Sum and rearrange the averaged m-error recursion over the Algorithm 2 horizon t=1,...,T to telescope the contraction, then divide by beta_2 T. The division uses the implicit beta_2 positive-domain prerequisite and the explicit loop/horizon adapter; T>0 follows from the node-count and horizon prerequisites.

Bound the first-iteration averaged stochastic-gradient error by sigma^2/n, giving the second line of Eq. (10). The paper's Section 4.2 initialization is printed without node superscripts; the named nodewise first-step adapter supplies the m_1^j interpretation required by Appendix D, and cross-node cancellation remains an explicit formal prerequisite beyond Assumption 7.

Under beta_2^2 <= beta_1 <= sqrt(beta_2), apply the v-recursion across the Algorithm 2 horizon, isolate the first stochastic v_1 error, and sum the remaining m-error terms through T-1. The sigma^2/(nT) initial term uses the named nodewise first-step adapter for the printed unsuperscripted initialization and the same explicit cross-node cancellation requirement. The finite averages and divisions use the loop/horizon and positive node-count prerequisites, while the contraction and 1/beta_1 terms also rely on the unstated beta-domain prerequisite.

Substitute the Eq. (10) m-error average into the v-error bound. The PDF moves from the T-1 m-error sum multiplied by (1-beta_1) to the T-sum bound in Eq. (10); formally this uses 0<=1-beta_1<=1 from the momentum-domain prerequisite and nonnegativity of the squared m-error terms before applying the Eq. (10) estimate.

Use beta_2^2 <= beta_1 <= sqrt(beta_2) to simplify the beta-dependent terms. Formally this simplification also requires 0<beta_2<=1, giving beta_1^2<=beta_2, beta_2<=1 for sigma^2/(nT) <= sigma^2/(beta_2 nT), and beta_2^2<=beta_1 for 1/beta_1 <= 1/beta_2^2; the paper does not state this domain separately.

Transport the final averaged-node v-error bound for \bar v_t through the sign-preserving sum/average update adapter and substitute it into the descent reduction. No equality between the squared errors of v_t^{\mathrm{sum}} and \bar v_t is asserted.

The paper now applies the printed beta_2=O(n^{1/2}T^{-1/2}), eta=O(n^{1/4}d^{-1/2}T^{-3/4}), and T>=n schedules and prints the rate.
